subject: Re: Hosted API: Starter → Enterprise token schedule & billing ops
messages:
From: Sasha Lee <sasha@finapps.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: hosted API annual token options and payment cadence

Hi Jordan,

Quick intro — I'm Sasha, head of platform at FinApps. We're evaluating Redwood for customer-facing features and expect to hit ~1B tokens/mo in steady state by Q4 next year. Procurement asked me to gather options for a 12-month commitment with tiered discounts (starter/growth/enterprise) and to understand how burst capacity and overage billing would work.

Can you send a short matrix with:
- Starter/Growth/Enterprise commit bands (tokens/month and annual totals)
- Unit price per 1k tokens at each band and cumulative discounting rules
- Overage behavior and negotiated grace buffers
- Billing cadence options (monthly invoice vs. net-30/60 prepay)
- Any SLA credits or minimum throughput guarantees tied to tiers

Would prefer something we can share with finance — XLS or PDF is great. We may have questions on data retention and audit logs but want to nail pricing first.

Thanks,
Sasha
Head of Platform | FinApps

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Sasha Lee <sasha@finapps.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API annual token options and payment cadence

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear brief. Attaching a compact spreadsheet (redwood-token-schedule-v2.xlsx) that lays out three recommended bands: Starter (50M/mo), Growth (250M/mo), Enterprise (1B+/mo) with corresponding effective per-1k-token prices, burst credit mechanics, and billing templates. Key notes up front:

- Discounts are volume-based and applied against monthly consumption within the contract period (not retroactive to previous months).
- We propose a 10% buffer for the Growth band and 5% for Enterprise as an initial grace to reduce churn on traffic spikes; overages are billed at the next tier rate unless you opt into capped overage.
- Payment: default monthly invoicing Net-30. We can support prepay with a 1.5% discount to effective rate for annual prepayment.

I'm copying Marissa and Ben for margin & ops constraints — Marissa can confirm approval thresholds for deeper discounts; Ben can speak to burst capacity and SLA addenda.

If this looks good, we can convert the spreadsheet into a short commercial proposal and include the SLA addendum (SLA_addendum_FinApps.pdf).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-token-schedule-v2.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API annual token options and payment cadence

Thanks Jordan — reviewed the spreadsheet. A couple of commercial constraints to flag before we send:

- Enterprise band discounts above 35% require CRO approval; propose we hold Enterprise at max 30% and offer staircase rebates (performance-based) that unlock up to 5% more at usage thresholds.
- For Growth band, the 10% buffer is fine but recommend capped overage at +15% of committed tokens at a +25% per-token surcharge instead of full next-tier billing — easier for finance to model.
- Prepay discount: 1.5% seems low for large credits; suggest 2.5% for > $250k annual prepay.

I also added comment rows in the XLS about minimum quarterly reporting requirements for usage reconciliation. If we include an SLA credit table, make sure incident credit multipliers don't exceed 10% of monthly invoice for Enterprise.

-M
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API annual token options and payment cadence

Quick operational notes:

- Burst capacity: for Enterprise we can enable guaranteed burst pools (separate reserved capacity) billed as committed capacity add-on or metered at a reduced overage. For Growth we'll do the 10% buffer as a soft limit with telemetry alerts and automated fallback to a compatible lower-cost model for degraded latency.
- Implementation: need a mutually agreed MAP (mutual action plan) with expected traffic curves to size the reserved pool. Recommend we include a one-page MAP in the proposal template.
- Attach SLA_addendum_FinApps.pdf if they ask for data retention/audit logs — that's a legal/infra attachment; legal will need to review any changes.

Ben Carter
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Sasha Lee <sasha@finapps.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, procurement@acme.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: Starter → Enterprise token schedule & billing ops

Sasha — following up with an updated package based on internal feedback. Highlights:

- Starter: 50M tokens/mo (annualized 600M) — standard support, no reserved burst. Price: $0.95 per 1k tokens.
- Growth: 250M tokens/mo (3B annual) — 10% soft buffer, capped overage at +15% billed at +25% surcharge. Price: $0.62 per 1k tokens.
- Enterprise: 1B tokens/mo baseline (12B annual) — up to 30% discount baseline, staircase rebates to 35% at 150% utilization. Guaranteed burst pool available as add-on. Price: $0.42 per 1k tokens (baseline).
- Prepay: annual prepayment >$250k gets 2.5% additional discount; monthly Net-30 is default.
- SLA credits capped at 10% monthly invoice for Enterprise; MAP and quarterly usage reconciliation included.

Attached: redwood-token-schedule-v2.xlsx (updated), SLA_addendum_FinApps.pdf. Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up on Tue to walk through the MAP and procurement checklist?

If procurement provides preferred billing cadence or a PO template, we can cut a formal offer.

Thanks — Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-token-schedule-v2.xlsx, SLA_addendum_FinApps.pdf
